subject: Post-demo: SLA, concurrency & burst profile — clarifying tradeoffs for deploy mode
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Anita Sharma <anita@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo recap — SLA & concurrency clarifying questions

Hi Anita / Lester —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can size the pilot and make a deployment recommendation (Hosted API vs Dedicated).

High-level from your side: checkout flows are latency-sensitive (checkout auth + pricing) and product discovery has bursty batch workloads (search rerank). We want to confirm numbers so engineering can propose an appropriate pilot config.

Can you confirm the following for the pilot / production target?
- P95 latency target for checkout requests (target SLO) — is 150ms P95 acceptable, or do you need sub-100ms?
- Average sustained QPS during business hours and expected burst QPS (e.g., sustained 50 qps, bursts to 800 qps for 30s)?
- Typical request size: avg tokens / request (prompt + expected response).
- Concurrency model per user/session (are requests single-shot or do you hold KV cache across multiple calls in a session?)
- Any strict data residency or network requirements that would push this to Private VPC / on‑prem?

Quick notes on tradeoffs we mentioned:
- Hosted API: fastest to start; generally handles bursts well but tail latency during big bursts can increase if we rely on multi-customer shared pools. Good for pilot if you can tolerate a modest increase in tail latency.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPUs give predictable throughput and tighter tail latency; recommended if you need consistent P95 < 120ms under bursts or have high, sustained throughput with predictable QPS.
- Private (VPC/on‑prem): mainly for strict compliance/regulatory needs — more setup timeline.

Attachments: I attached a small pilot-qps-sample.csv you can fill with per-endpoint traffic and our draft SLA (redwood-sla-draft.pdf) for reference.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm numbers above.
2) Tech deep-dive with Ben (our infra lead) — 45m — we can do Tues/Wed next week.
3) We provide two pilot options (Hosted pilot with burst tuning; Dedicated single‑tenant pool) with cost/latency estimates.

Thanks —
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Anita Sharma <anita@fastretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-01T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — SLA & concurrency clarifying questions

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below — happy to fill the CSV once I have a little time.

- P95 target for checkout: ideally <= 120ms. Sub-100ms would be great but not a hard blocker at launch.
- Sustained QPS (US peak hours): 60 qps on average for checkout endpoints. Burst profile: 700–900 qps spikes for 20–45s during promotional pushes and peak browsing.
- Typical tokens: checkout prompts are small — ~70–150 tokens total. Search/rerank requests average ~250 tokens. Response sizes are generally short (20–60 tokens).
- Concurrency: for checkout we tend to make single-shot calls. For discovery flows, sessions may hit the model multiple times within short windows but no extensive KV reuse across minutes.
- Data residency: everything must remain in the US; we do not require on‑prem, but we do need strong audit logs and a SOC2 report.

Given the P95 requirement + high burst amplitude, we are leaning toward Dedicated if the latency estimates hold up. But we would like to try a Hosted pilot first to confirm behavior and validate integration velocity, with a clear escape plan to Dedicated.

I’ll try to complete the CSV by tomorrow EOD. Can we schedule the tech deep‑dive for Wed 12/2 10am PT?

Best,
Anita Sharma
Head of Platform Engineering, FastRetail
Anita.Sharma@fastretail.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Anita Sharma <anita@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-01T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — SLA & concurrency clarifying questions

Thanks Anita (and Tessa). Two quick technical clarifications so we size the pilot correctly.

1) Burst shape: are those 700–900 qps spikes simultaneous single-token fan-out (e.g., many users hitting one endpoint) or are they spread across a few endpoints? If you have a short CSV with timestamps/sample windows that would help.
2) Warm KV/cache reuse: you noted no extensive KV reuse; for discovery rerank, are there repeated prefixes within a user session we can benefit from (even a 5–10% reuse helps).
3) P95 target: you gave <=120ms for checkout. To be conservative, can we confirm an internal target of 100–120ms? If you require 100ms P95 under 900 qps bursts, Dedicated is the safer choice — Hosted can meet that at lower sustained QPS, but tail depends on cross-tenant mixing and queueing.

Pilot plan (technical):
- Hosted pilot option: 2 weeks, small traffic ramp (5–15% of traffic routed through Redwood hosted pool), service-level measurement with tracing and token-level cost reports. Fallback: route to Dedicated if P95 degrades >20% over baseline.
- Dedicated pilot option: 2-week reserved pool with autoscaling headroom sized to handle 900 qps bursts with P95 headroom. Longer provisioning lead time but consistent tail performance.

For the tech deep-dive on Wed 12/2 10am PT I’ll bring:
- latency profiles for similar customers
- recommended Dedicated pool sizes and cost deltas vs Hosted
- proposal for Canary routing and fallback rules

If Wed 10am PT works for you, I’ll send the calendar invite and a short agenda.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
